title: Witches
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: An award-winning anthology of stories about witches around the world. In the first, a British girl, Nicola, falls for Mimar, a young man at a bazaar in a small far-western Asian country, and years later returns with wealth and 'the secret of the world' to take deadly revenge. Other tales follow a shaman defending a South American rainforest, a witch in a European mountain country trying to save humans from themselves at a terrible price, a girl in modern Japan who may be tricked out of her name, a child searching for her cat, and a story drawn from Okinawan myth (Seven Seas blurb; ANN Spring 2022 Manga Guide).
life_message: Humans have cut themselves off from nature, and witches stand at the threshold between people and the living world.

content.note: Nicola's revenge is deadly; body-horror elements (ANN); Body Horror tag (AniList), Revenge (MU).
Abstract, macabre magic (ANN); Mind Break category (MU).

frames.concerns: Witchcraft and shamanism presented as truth and power.

Witches, spirits and shamans as heroes.

frames.aligns: Critique of modern technology and excess.

Cultural portrayals of 'far west Asia' and South America (to verify).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Wisdom held by witches, not rulers.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Folk magic and myth over modern separation from nature (ANN).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Inner emotions awaken the 'witch in the heart' (MU description).

folkways.japan: One tale draws on Okinawan mythology; the collection reflects a Japanese animist sense of spirit in nature.

delivery.evidence: ANN: Silverman finds stories sometimes 'on the nose' and philosophically heavy-handed; another reviewer says it does not overexplain.
delivery.note: Reviewers split on whether the environmental message is overstated; the modern, nature-separated view is not given its own advocate (to verify).

winners_losers: Nature and witches carry the story's sympathy; the rainforest shaman fails and the mountain witch succeeds at a terrible price (ANN).
